records.name: multi_sword
records.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: AAA first-person medieval game sword modeling turnaround reference, 6 consistent orthographic views of ONE object.
Primary request: create a high-resolution 3D weapon artist's reference sheet of a realistic worn late medieval hand-and-a-half sword, based on the sword in the attached reference (style/subject guidance only; do not include its hands, shield or environment).
Composition: landscape 3 columns by 2 rows, six equal spacious panels, dark neutral charcoal plain background, studio soft key and rim illumination, no floor. Each panel labeled small clean English at bottom: FRONT, BACK, LEFT, RIGHT, TOP, BOTTOM, in this exact reading order. Front and back show the whole sword upright, point up, pommel down. Left/right are genuinely edge-on showing blade thickness, no 3/4 cheating. Top looks straight down blade from the point; bottom looks up from the pommel. Maintain IDENTICAL physical geometry, materials and wear patterns in all views. Main front/back occupy almost entire panel height with adequate margins. Smaller top/bottom cross-section views should be enlarged for legibility.
Subject geometry: total length 127 cm: 98 cm slender straight double-edged tapering blade with a recessed narrow fuller through upper 70 percent; blade base 5.4 cm wide tapering to a sharp tip. Hammer-forged blue-gray steel with bright honed edge bevels, subtle lengthwise grinding marks and restrained fine pitting; clearly steel, not gray plastic. Guard 23 cm across, simple solid gently swept quillons, flattened diamond section, slightly downward-swept graceful ends, no decorative protrusions. Dark worn charcoal-brown leather grip 20 cm long, subtle spiral seams over an oval wooden core, compressed leather near finger contact. Steel collar and narrow ferrule. Compact pear/fishtail steel pommel with grounded medieval craftsmanship, no giant ball. The weapon is functional, elegant, restrained; believable hand proportions for a first-person game.
Materials: photoreal PBR quality, irregular edge wear, restrained roughness variation, subtle polished highlights, dark creases of leather, crisp fine bevels. Workmanship should have coherent handmade detail, not perfectly uniform procedural repeated rings.
Constraints: exactly one sword identity in all six views; no hands, no characters, no sheath, no runes or magical glow, no extra weapons, no broad fantasy blade. Design readable for actual 3D reconstruction. Very high detail.

records.name: multi_shield
records.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: AAA first-person medieval game round shield modeling reference, six directional views of exactly the SAME physical shield.
Create a very high detail 3 columns by 2 rows contact sheet, six EQUAL SQUARE panels. Plain charcoal background. Soft neutral studio lighting with an edge light revealing real rolled steel and leather grain. No ground, no hands, no characters.
Panel labels FRONT, BACK, LEFT, RIGHT, TOP, BOTTOM in reading order. FRONT faces the opponent, BACK faces the owner and clearly reveals the two real leather enarmes. LEFT/RIGHT are true orthographic views from the left/right edge with their corresponding rim and projected handles. TOP/BOTTOM are true orthographic edge views from straight above/below, NOT front or back views and NOT 3/4. In every panel the full silhouette is present with consistent physical scale; no crop. Side and top views should honestly show the shallow dish and leather handle standoff, no impossible giant handle depth.
Subject: a grounded realistic 82 cm round wooden medieval shield for the LEFT arm, visually related to the attached image (reference for overall design and quality only). Seven individual dark weathered oak boards, broad lengthwise grain, slightly uneven dark gaps, small chips at edges; shallow domed profile about 25 mm depth, 18 mm board thickness. Rolled aged blue-gray steel U-shaped rim about 28 mm wide, restrained bright scuffed bevels, rivets spaced around both sides, convincing metal thickness not a huge tire. Plain low hammered steel central boss on FRONT ONLY, 15 cm diameter, attached with six rivets. Exposed wood, no paint or heraldry.
On BACK: exactly two sturdy dark chestnut brown leather enarmes, mechanically credible and FIXED at both ends to riveted leather mounting tabs lying FLAT on the board. Their curved middle sections stand away from the wood for a hand/forearm. A narrower oval hand grip at viewer's RIGHT of rear center, and a wider adjustable forearm cuff to viewer's LEFT; angled modestly to support a left forearm running diagonally from bottom-left to the grip. Wrist clearance 8-10 cm. Strap ends with visible stitching and dull iron domed fasteners. Forearm cuff has a small rectangular iron buckle, punched holes and a tucked end. Each loop is real continuous THICK FLAT LEATHER, not a floating stick, not a pipe, not a triangular tent.
Materials: natural irregular wood grain and erosion, rich dark brown wood, creases and tension in worn brown leather, subtle sweat polish and wear, patinated forged steel with credible bright edges and slight denting. Real PBR photoreal product render, refined near-camera game asset quality.
Constraints: exact same shield and material landmarks in all six views. Do not invent a new object for each view. TOP and BOTTOM must be edge elevations. No glow, skulls, spikes, decals, letters on the shield, no spare weapons.

records.name: multi_sword_corrected
records.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Edit target: attached sword six-view sheet.
Keep the EXACT sword identity and the FRONT BACK LEFT RIGHT photographs unchanged in design, patina, dimensions, slender blade, recessed fuller, brown-black oval leather grip and pear pommel. Re-layout all six into equal 3 by 2 panels with same charcoal background and small English labels FRONT BACK LEFT RIGHT TOP BOTTOM. Do not change existing four correct elevations.
CRITICAL fix ONLY the directional error of the last two views: TOP must be a true orthographic camera positioned on the blade's long axis directly beyond the tip, looking down at the crossguard and pommel. The long blade is foreshortened to its little diamond cross section; the crossguard reads as a horizontal bar in the image and blade thickness/grip fit are visible. BOTTOM must be a true orthographic camera on the same long axis beyond the pommel, looking straight upward; show an oval/faceted pommel end face centered with the crossguard horizontal beyond it. The blade is hidden behind the pommel. TOP and BOTTOM should NOT show the length of the sword, NOT have a perspective vanishing-point long blade, and NOT both show the same 3/4 view. Magnify the top/bottom axial views so crossguard spans half of each panel width. These are technical axial product views, physically plausible, not tilted for drama. Leave enough margins. Consistent object and high quality photoreal metal/materials in all six.
